AI Project
Tang (ทาง) - Asia Trip Planner in Prolog and Python
Project Description (one page)

Tang (ทาง) is a desktop Asia trip planner for travellers starting from Thailand (Bangkok Suvarnabhumi BKK, Bangkok Don Mueang DMK, Chiang Mai, or Phuket) and visiting Japan, South Korea, China, or Singapore. Given the departure city, destination (or "Anywhere"), travel dates, number of days, group size, budget, interests, pace, and ranking preference, the program plans international flights with connections, chooses 1 to 4 cities inside the destination country, schedules daily attractions, calculates total costs, and explains the reasons behind every recommendation.

1. Program Structure

All reasoning and decision-making are written in SWI-Prolog (prolog/trip.pl). Python is used only for the user interface, map rendering, and optional fare lookup:

  • prolog/trip.pl: Knowledge base and logic rules (1,102 lines). Uses only standard Prolog features from Clocksin & Mellish (facts, rules, arithmetic, lists, cut, dynamic predicates, findall, insertion sort, and graph search).
  • backend/planner.py and backend/geo.py: Connects Python to SWI-Prolog using pyswip, validates user inputs, sends queries to plan_trip/11, and converts Prolog lists into Python dictionaries.
  • backend/live_prices.py: Optionally fetches real flight fares from the Aviasales API (cached in cache/fares.json so demos work offline) and passes them to Prolog as live_fare/3 and live_departure/2 facts.
  • app.py and ui/*: Desktop application built with PySide6 (Qt6) with two pages: a search page (trip form and a clickable Asia map) and a results page with a New search button to go back. The results page shows the live Prolog query, replays Prolog's search steps on the map, and displays tickets, day-by-day plans, costs, and booking links.

2. Knowledge Base Data

CountriesCitiesAirportsFlights Ground RoutesAttractionsHotelsBudget Airlines
5 (1 origin, 4 dest.)151362 18 (both ways)107 (7 types)1111

The knowledge base covers Thailand (Bangkok's two airports Suvarnabhumi BKK and Don Mueang DMK, linked by twin/2, plus Chiang Mai and Phuket), Japan (Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Sapporo), South Korea (Seoul, Busan, Jeju), China (Shanghai, Beijing, Xi'an), and Singapore. It also stores Thai passport visa-free limits, seasonal price changes (such as cherry blossom season, Golden Week, and rainy season), and Thai holiday surcharges (Songkran, October school break, and New Year).

3. Main Features

  • Trip inputs: 4 departure airports (BKK, DMK, CNX, HKT), 3 to 21 days, 1 to 6 people, group budget from ฿ 5,000 to ฿ 300,000, 7 interest categories (food, culture, nature, beach, shopping, adventure, nightlife), 3 paces (relaxed: fewer cities, longer stays; normal; packed: more cities, shorter stays), and 4 preferences (cheapest, fastest, fewest flights, balanced).
  • Extra constraints checked in Prolog: maximum flight changes (direct, 1 change, 2 changes), airline type (any, budget, full-service), avoid night flights (22:00 to 06:00), hotel level (budget, mid-range, luxury), ground transport mode (any, fast, no night rides), and picking specific cities to visit.
  • "Anywhere" mode: Prolog evaluates all four destination countries and ranks the top three trips by value.
  • Explanations and map replay: Every plan includes a list of reasons produced by Prolog (budget fit, flight connections, overnight savings, visa rules, seasonal tips, and a note when the flight home lands at Bangkok's other airport) and animates the search trace on the map.

The AI Concepts to Apply in this Project (at least two pages)

The AI logic in Tang is implemented in prolog/trip.pl using the concepts from Programming in Prolog (Clocksin & Mellish). No SWI-Prolog shortcut predicates such as aggregate_all, keysort, maplist, or -> are used. The main AI concepts applied in this project are described below.

1. Knowledge Representation (Facts and Rules)

Domain data is stored as Prolog facts separate from the planning rules. Main fact predicates include country/4, city/7, home/1, twin/2 (Bangkok's two airports), airport/2 (UTC offsets), flight/6, ground/5, stay/2, attraction/5, stay_range/3, visa_free/2, busy/3, thai_holiday/3, highlight/3, warning/3, overnight/1, and low_cost/1. Because the rules query these facts declaratively, new cities, flights, or attractions can be added without changing any search or planning code.

2. Best-First Search for Flight Routes

Finding the best flight route (up to 3 legs) is implemented as Best-First Search in best_routes/5, bf/5, visit/6, and shortest/3 (following go3 in Section 7.9). Each partial route in the frontier has the form r(Cost, Here, Clock, Visited, Legs). At every step, shortest/3 removes the lowest-cost partial route and expands it. Because every cost function only increases as more flights are added, the first K routes that reach the destination are guaranteed to be the K best routes. 

path_cost(cheapest, Legs, C) : sum of flight prices
path_cost(fastest,  Legs, C) : total elapsed minutes from first take-off to last landing
path_cost(fewest,   Legs, C) : number of legs * 1,000,000 + sum of prices
path_cost(balanced, Legs, C) : sum of prices + elapsed minutes * 10

During expansion, Prolog avoids cycles (\+ member(Next, Seen)), prevents outbound trips from routing back through Thailand (back_to_thailand/3), and checks time-zone connections in UTC (to_utc/3 and departure/5) so every layover is at least 90 minutes and at most 12 hours (720 minutes).

3. Depth-First Search Comparison

For comparison, trip.pl also includes a depth-first flight search with a trail (fly/3). Depth-first search must find every valid route and sort them to pick the best two, whereas best-first search stops as soon as the best two routes arrive. Running compare_search/5 in SWI-Prolog (for April with default options) gives the following step counts:

RouteDFS (Cheapest)BFS (Cheapest)Saved DFS (Fastest)BFS (Fastest)Saved
Bangkok -> Tokyo544124.1%543240.7%
Bangkok -> Seoul524023.1%523042.3%
Chiang Mai -> Tokyo653644.6%653250.8%
Phuket -> Tokyo624035.5%623641.9%
Chiang Mai -> Osaka653644.6%653743.1%
Phuket -> Beijing623740.3%624724.2%
Don Mueang -> Tokyo3651-41.7%3651-41.7%

Best-first search does less work on every route from Suvarnabhumi, Chiang Mai and Phuket. Don Mueang is the exception: only a few budget flights leave it, so depth-first search has little to try (36 steps), while best-first search keeps a sorted frontier of partial routes and does more work (51 steps). Best-first search pays off when there are many routes to choose from.

2
The AI Concepts to Apply in this Project (continued)

4. Dynamic Database, Memoization, and Live Facts

Prolog's dynamic predicates (assertz/1 and retract/1) are used in four places:

  • Memoization (flight_memo/4): Many city tours share the same arrival or departure airport. best_flights/4 saves the top 2 flight routes for each (From, To, Pref) pair so Prolog searches each airport pair only once.
  • User options (option/2): Extra choices arrive as a list such as [max_flights(1), hotel(luxury), cities([tokyo, kyoto])]. Using the univ operator =.. (Section 6.5), store_options/1 asserts each item as option(Name, Value), and opt/2 reads it with a cut-guarded fallback to default_option/2.
  • Search trace (explored/2, steps/1): Records each explored flight edge and step count so the UI can replay the search on the map.
  • Live fares (live_fare/3, live_departure/2): Python can assert real Aviasales prices and departure times before querying. flight_price/5 and departs/3 use cuts to prefer live facts and fall back to seasonal sample prices when offline.

5. Generate-and-Test and Constraint Checking

Complete trips are built by candidate/8 using generate-and-test (Chapter 4). Prolog picks an arrival airport in the target country, gets the best outbound flights, generates a domestic tour of up to 4 cities with round_tour/4 (depth-first search over linked/5), checks that the final city has an international airport, gets return flights to either Bangkok airport (home_airport/2 uses twin/2), and calls build_plan/11. Several constraints prune invalid plans early:

  • Flight and ground filters: airline_ok/3 extracts the two-letter carrier code using atom_chars/2 and checks low_cost/1; daytime_ok/1 rejects take-offs between 22:00 and 06:00 when requested; ground_ok/1 filters out overnight rides or buses according to the user's choice.
  • Picked cities and gateway rule (chosen_ok/2): When the user selects specific cities, the tour must visit only those cities. If a picked city has no international airport (such as Kyoto), end_ok/3 allows an adjacent airport city (Osaka) as a 1-night gateway stopover.
  • Day sharing (share_days/4): Every city must receive at least its minimum stay from stay_range/3 (adjusted by pace: -1 day for packed, +1 for relaxed). If there are not enough days, the tour fails and Prolog backtracks. Extra days are assigned one by one to the city with the most room left (MaxDays - DaysSoFar).
  • Budget filtering (affordable/3): Plans within the user's budget are kept first. If no plan fits the budget, Prolog still returns the closest plans and reports how much over budget they are.
3
The AI Concepts to Apply in this Project (continued)

6. Scoring, Ranking, and "Anywhere" Selection

After findall/3 collects all candidate plans, score/3 assigns a numeric key to each plan (smaller is better) and adds a penalty for empty days with no planned activities: 

cheapest : K0 = TotalCost
fastest  : K0 = FlightMinutes * 1000 + TotalCost
fewest   : K0 = TotalFlightLegs * 10,000,000 + TotalCost
balanced : K0 = TotalCost + FlightMinutes * 10 - Enjoyment * 1500
score    : K  = K0 + FreeDays * TotalCost // TripDays

Plans are sorted with insertion sort (insort/2, Section 7.7). To keep Plans A, B, and C useful as real alternatives, different/3 keeps only plans that visit different city sets. In "Anywhere" mode, best_per_country/4 picks the single best plan for each country and ranks countries by TotalCost - Enjoyment * 3000, treating each matching attraction as worth ฿3,000.

7. Daily Activity Scheduling and Overnight Travel

Available sightseeing hours depend on travel times: arrival_hours/2 counts from 1 hour after landing until 21:00, leaving_hours/2 counts from 09:00 until 3 hours before take-off, and moving_hours/2 subtracts road travel time from 8 hours. pick/6 and fit/4 place attractions matching the user's interests first, then other attractions, fitting up to 3 unvisited places per day. Overnight rides (night_bus, night_train, night_ferry) are detected by on_board/3, which removes one hotel night and gives 7 free hours the next morning.

8. Rule-Based Explanations

For each chosen plan, reasons/11 builds a list of reason terms (such as [under_budget, Spare], [direct, out, Code, From, To], [overnight], [gateway, City], [visa_ok, Country, Days], [other_airport, Home, Land] from twin_reason/3 when the trip ends at the other Bangkok airport, and seasonal highlights or warnings). Python simply turns these terms into readable sentences for the user.

 335  clock_minutes(HHMM, M) :- M is (HHMM // 100) * 60 + HHMM mod 100.

 337  to_utc(City, HHMM, T) :-
 338      airport(City, Zone),
 339      clock_minutes(HHMM, M),
 340      T is M - Zone * 60.
 341  
 342  local_time(City, T, Day, Clock) :-
 343      airport(City, Zone),
 344      L is T + Zone * 60,
 345      Day is L // 1440,
 346      Clock is L mod 1440.

 348  departure(start, City, HHMM, Dep, 0) :-
 349      to_utc(City, HHMM, Dep).
 350  departure(landed(Arr), City, HHMM, Dep, Wait) :-
 351      to_utc(City, HHMM, T),
 352      W is (T - Arr) mod 1440,
 353      enough_time(W, Wait),
 354      Wait =< 720,
 355      Dep is Arr + Wait.
 356  
 357  enough_time(W, W) :- W >= 90, !.
 358  enough_time(W, W1) :- W1 is W + 1440.

  86      def fare_routes(self, origin: str, destination: str) -> tuple[list, list]:
  87          countries = ({c for c in self.countries if c != "thailand"} if destination == "anywhere" else {destination})
  88          targets = {c["id"] for c in self._map["cities"] if c["country"] in countries}
  89          ends = {origin, "bangkok", "don_mueang"}
  90          pairs = set()
  91          for f in self._map["flights"]:
  92              a, b = f["from"], f["to"]
  93              if (a in ends and b in targets) or (b in ends and a in targets) or (origin in (a, b) and {a, b} <= ends):
  94                  pairs.add((a, b))
  95          outbound = sorted(p for p in pairs if p[0] == origin or (p[0] in ends and p[1] in targets))
  96          inbound = sorted(p for p in pairs if p not in outbound)
  97          return outbound, inbound

 125

 150      def option_terms(self, options: dict, destination: str) -> list[str]:
 151          terms = []
 152          if options.get("max_flights") in (1, 2):
 153              terms.append(f'max_flights({options["max_flights"]})')
 154          if options.get("airlines") in ("budget", "full"):
 155              terms.append(f'airlines({options["airlines"]})')
 156          if options.get("night_flights") == "avoid":
 157              terms.append("night_flights(avoid)")
 158          if options.get("hotel") in ("budget", "luxury"):
 159              terms.append(f'hotel({options["hotel"]})')
 160          if options.get("getting_around") in ("fast", "no_night"):
 161              terms.append(f'getting_around({options["getting_around"]})')
 162          picked = [c for c in options.get("cities", []) if c in self.cities
 163                    and (destination == "anywhere" or self.cities[c]["country"] == destination)]
 164          if picked:
 165              terms.append(f'cities([{",".join(picked)}])')
 166          return terms

 169      def _name(self, city_id: str) -> str:
 170          return self.cities[city_id]["name"]
 171  
 172      def _clock(self, city_id: str, utc_minutes: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
 173          local = utc_minutes + self.cities[city_id]["zone"] * 60
 174          day, clock = divmod(local, 1440)
 175          return f"{clock // 60:02d}:{clock % 60:02d}", day
 176  
 177      def _legs(self, rows) -> list[dict]:
 178          legs = []
 179          first_day = None
 180          for code, frm, to, dep, arr, price, wait in rows:
 181              dep_clock, dep_day = self._clock(frm, dep)
 182              arr_clock, arr_day = self._clock(to, arr)
 183              if first_day is None:
 184                  first_day = dep_day
 185              legs.append({
 186                  "code": code, "from": frm, "to": to, "price": price, "wait": wait,
 187                  "minutes": arr - dep,
 188                  "depart": dep_clock, "arrive": arr_clock,
 189                  "departDay": dep_day - first_day, "arriveDay": arr_day - first_day,
 190              })
 191          return legs

 309      def _empty_reason(self, origin, destination, flight_options, plans, days, pace) -> str | None:
 310          if flight_options == 0:
 311              where = "any country" if destination == "anywhere" else self.countries[destination]["name"]
 312              return (f"No flights from {self._name(origin)} reach {where} with these flight options. "
 313                      "Try allowing more changes, any airline, or night flights.")
 314          if plans == 0:
 315              return (f"No plan fits {days} days at a {pace} pace with these options. "
 316                      "Add days, choose a faster pace, allow more flight changes or any airline, "
 317                      "or pick different cities.")
 318          return None
